title: For a designer
reader: an editorial designer who lays out non-fiction books and long features
judges: Do the pages, maps and pictures carry the argument?
why_you: You make long arguments readable for a living. Where a picture should replace a paragraph here, or a paragraph a picture, you will see it before anyone else.

chapters_note: Chapters proposed by the storyteller (team/storyteller/review-questions.md), a proposal until the editor rules on the length per page; the 'short of time' chapter is developer@'s proposal.

questions.q: Did the maps help you understand, or did you read past them?
Which figure would you redraw first, and how?
Where should a picture replace a paragraph, or a paragraph replace a picture?
Would you know a map was coming before you met it?
Can you picture the talk from this chapter? What image is missing?
Which of the team's visual choices would you keep in the book's own design?
Where does the page feel crowded or thin?
